method: The listed basmati rice quantity is the dry, uncooked weight. Follow the cooking and assembly steps below for this measured portion.

Start the 75g basmati rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.

Peel and finely slice the 90g onion and deseed and thinly slice the 90g mixed peppers. Cut the 170g lean pork loin into pieces no larger than 2cm on a separate board. Wash hands, the board and knife after handling the raw meat; do not rinse it.
Mix 20g light mayonnaise, 5ml lemon juice and 1g dried parsley in a small bowl. Keep this dressing cold until serving; it is not a cooking sauce and must not be simmered in the pan.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the lean pork loin in one layer and cook for 10–12 minutes, turning regularly. Lower the heat if the outside browns too quickly. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must reach 70°C for 2 minutes. Keep cooking if it has not reached that endpoint; the suggested time is a guide. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g onion and 90g mixed peppers and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.

Return the cooked lean pork loin and its juices to the pan and stir through. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, stirring to distribute the heat. Spoon the pan mixture over the freshly cooked rice. Take the pan off the heat and spoon the cold dressing over each serving; do not return it to the hob. Serve immediately.
